Detects secret, token, or password labels followed by 32 to 64 hexadecimal characters. This is a format and length heuristic, not a measured entropy score. Quoted JSON keys and values are supported.

Detect literal password assignments including common camel-case fields, YAML/JSON/env and := assignments. Exclude explicit UI-label identifiers, unquoted property references, callbacks, types, shell expansions and complete placeholders per candidate. Ambiguous bare literals remain a format heuristic; no file/category allowlists.
Detect user:password authority components in connection URLs; exclude username-only URLs and interpolated credentials.
Detect a base64 credential following an explicit Authorization: Basic header.
Detect a signed JWT-shaped value with a JSON header, payload and signature; no token is authenticated or sent to an issuer.
Detect labelled symmetric/encryption hex keys. Public-key and sealing-public-key identifiers are not generic key fields; their presence never exempts a separate secret.
Detect asymmetric JWK private member d together with kty in the same object or object fragment, in either order. A public-only JWK does not match.
Detect SQL IDENTIFIED BY, IDENTIFIED WITH/VIA plugin BY/AS, and PostgreSQL PASSWORD literals. No query execution or model calls; variable references and placeholders are excluded.

Detect explicit --password/-Password arguments, OpenSSL pass: sources and attached MySQL -p literals. Environment/file sources, interactive flags and shell variables do not match; other commands do not interpret generic -p as a password.
Detect 58-character, uppercase Base32 NATS NKEY seed shapes (SA/SC/SN/SO/SU/SX). Public NKEYs do not match. Exposure detection validates format, not CRC or whether a credential is active.

Detect one layer of Base64-encoded PEM private-key headers with a bounded body and line wrapping. Public-key/certificate headers do not match. This is exposure detection, not cryptographic key validation or recursive decoding.
